Coefficients of the categorical = "level" start in the EM's design

Source: R/cellgloc_categorical.R
dot-gloc_level_B.Rd

The categorical EM's second start is the robust start of categorical = "level", whose design has a level for the missing value; the EM's design has none. Under treatment coding, the default for an unordered factor, that level adds its own columns, which are 0 on every row whose value is known, and leaves the others unchanged: the rows of B for those columns are dropped. That holds exactly when the design of "level", evaluated at the EM's pseudo-rows, equals the EM's pseudo-row design in the EM's columns and is 0 in the others, which is what is checked. Otherwise – an ordered factor, whose polynomial coding changes with the number of levels, or sum contrasts – the start's fitted means are carried over: the coefficients are the least-squares fit of the EM's pseudo-row design to the fitted means the "level" start gives the same level combinations, with the coefficients of aliased columns at 0. Both routes give the pseudo-rows the start's fitted means, which is all the iteration uses of a start's coefficients; where both apply they agree up to rounding.

.gloc_level_B(B, Ulv, Up, lsq = FALSE)

Arguments

B

coefficients of the "level" design, one row per column of Ulv.

Ulv

that design at the pseudo-rows (.gloc_level_rows).

Up

the EM's pseudo-row design.

lsq

TRUE takes the least-squares route even where the rows can be dropped; for testing.

Value

a matrix with one row per column of Up.
